newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Transaero mulls share issue after 1996 H1 audit.
newsitem.headline: Transaero mulls share issue after 1996 H1 audit.

text.p: Russia's private AO Transaero airlines plans a share issue after its audit for the first half of 1996 is completed, a senior company official said on Monday.
Board member Alexei Andreyev said the share issue question would be resolved after Ernst & Young finished the audit. "We hope to get the audit results in three weeks," he told Reuters.
He said the issue's size and timing had yet to be decided.

Earlier this year, Transaero officials said the company planned to issue ordinary registered shares. They said Transaero had signed an agreement with ABN AMRO to make the Dutch bank the company's registrar from the second half of 1996.
It is not clear whether the issue will be a public offering or a private placement.
At the beginning of this year, Russia's Alliance-Menatep and Ernst & Young audited the company and put its assets at $160 million. Alliance-Menatep will manage the share issue.
Russia's Aeroflot International Airlines owns five percent of Transaero. Employees own 15 percent of shares and the rest belongs to several Russian aircraft design bureaux and other shareholders.
